(CNN)  -- With his hands and feet shackled and his face obscured by his long hair, Chester Arthur Stiles made his initial court appearance in Las Vegas, Nevada, on Wednesday morning on charges stemming from the videotaped rape of a 2-year-old girl. Chester Stiles appears Wednesday in a Las Vegas, Nevada, courtroom. Stiles, 37, was taken into custody Monday night after a Henderson, Nevada, police officer pulled over the white Buick Century he was driving. Prosecutors added a couple more charges before Wednesday's hearing, bringing the total to 23 felony counts, including a charge of lewdness with a minor, sexual assault and the use of a child in the production of pornography, according to a statement issued by the Clark County, Nevada, court. One of the lewdness charges stems from a 2004 incident, while the others are related to the videotape, the court said. Judge Deborah Lippis set November 19 as the date for the preliminary hearing. After the hearing, Stiles' court-appointed attorney said his client was overwhelmed by the public opinion in the case. "I think he's a little out of it," public defender Jeff Banks said. Jerry T. Donohue, the attorney for the girl's mother, told CNN that the child on the videotape was younger than 3 when the abuse occurred. The girl, who is now 7, was found last month after a nationwide search. The girl's mother said on "The Dr. Phil Show" Wednesday that she was "relieved" about Stiles' arrest, although it would have been "better if they found him dead." The woman said she will testify against Stiles if the case goes to court. She told Phil McGraw that her daughter remembers nothing about the videotaped assault and that she recently had a conversation with the girl about inappropriate touching. She said her daughter told her that if someone touched her inappropriately, the girl would scream and tell her mother. But, she told McGraw, "I don't trust anybody now." Although she is in a relationship with a man her daughter calls "Dad," she said, "I don't feel comfortable leaving her with him, nor with anybody else. ... I just cry and blame it on myself." Eight-and-a-half months pregnant, she said the incident has placed a lot of strain on her. Asked if she would rather not have known about the assault, she said, "Yes, I could have lived without knowing it." A former girlfriend of Stiles' said that, before the arrest, she lived in fear after going to police to identify the suspect after seeing enhanced photos from the videotape on the local news. "I've had my share of nightmares," Elaine Thomas told CNN's Nancy Grace. Thomas said she screamed when she recognized the photos on television and had no choice but to contact police about the man she had thought was a "weapons enthusiast" with only a minor criminal record.  Watch Thomas say how she felt when she saw the photos » . "How could I not tell them who that man was? That little girl suffered unimaginable things, and I knew for a fact it was him," Thomas said. Another former girlfriend of Stiles', Tina Allen, said this month she thinks she is the reason Stiles came in contact with the girl and is "mortified" by the allegations against him. "He said he'd been in the Navy and, you know, I was looking for a strong guy to represent to my sons what I thought they needed to be," Allen said. Allen said she took Stiles to a crowded apartment where her son and daughter lived. Also living in the apartment were a family friend and her daughter, the alleged assault victim. Todd Allen, Tina Allen's son, said he recognized his old apartment from scenes in the video.  E-mail to a friend . CNN's Ed Payne and Ted Rowlands contributed to this report.

LAS VEGAS, Nevada (CNN) — Chester Arthur Stiles appeared in court for the first time Wednesday morning with restraints on his wrists and ankles and long hair covering much of his face. He faces charges connected to the recorded sexual assault of a 2-year-old girl.

Stiles, 37, was arrested Monday night after an officer in Henderson, Nevada, stopped the white Buick Century he was driving.

Before Wednesday’s proceeding, prosecutors filed two additional charges, increasing the case to 23 felony counts. According to a statement from the Clark County court, the allegations include lewdness with a minor, sexual assault, and using a child to produce pornography. The court said one lewdness count concerns an incident from 2004, while the remaining counts are tied to the video.

Judge Deborah Lippis scheduled the preliminary hearing for November 19.

Following the appearance, court-appointed defense attorney Jeff Banks said Stiles was struggling with the intense public reaction to the case.

“I think he’s a little out of it,” Banks said.

Jerry T. Donohue, who represents the girl’s mother, told CNN that the child shown in the recording was under 3 years old when the alleged abuse took place. The girl, now 7, was located last month following a nationwide search.

Speaking Wednesday on “The Dr. Phil Show,” the child’s mother said she felt “relieved” that Stiles had been arrested, though she added that it would have been “better if they found him dead.” She said she would testify against him if the matter proceeds to trial.

The mother told Phil McGraw that her daughter has no memory of the recorded assault. She said they recently discussed inappropriate touching, and the girl told her she would scream and inform her mother if anyone touched her improperly.

Nevertheless, the mother said, “I don’t trust anybody now.”

Although she is involved with a man whom her daughter calls “Dad,” the woman said she does not feel safe leaving the child with him or anyone else. She added that she cries and holds herself responsible.

The woman, who was eight and a half months pregnant, said the situation had caused her significant stress. When asked whether she would have preferred never to learn of the assault, she replied, “Yes, I could have lived without knowing it.”

Elaine Thomas, one of Stiles’ former girlfriends, said she had been afraid before his arrest because she contacted police after recognizing him in enhanced images from the video that were broadcast by local news outlets.

“I’ve had my share of nightmares,” Thomas told CNN’s Nancy Grace.

Thomas said she screamed when she identified the person in the televised pictures. She felt compelled to notify authorities about the man she had previously regarded as a “weapons enthusiast” whose criminal history was relatively minor.

“How could I not tell them who that man was?” Thomas said. “That little girl suffered unimaginable things, and I knew for a fact it was him.”

Another former girlfriend, Tina Allen, said earlier that month that she believed she may have been responsible for bringing Stiles into contact with the girl. She said she was “mortified” by the accusations.

Allen explained that Stiles had told her he served in the Navy. She said she had wanted a strong male figure who could provide her sons with what she believed they needed.

Allen said she brought Stiles to a crowded apartment occupied by her son and daughter. A family friend and that friend’s daughter—the alleged victim—also lived there.

Tina Allen’s son, Todd Allen, said scenes in the recording appeared to show his former apartment.

CNN’s Ed Payne and Ted Rowlands contributed to the report.

Stiles appeared before a judge in jail clothing and restraints, facing 23 felony charges. The complaint included 11 counts of sexual assault of a child younger than 14, 11 counts of lewdness with a child younger than 14 and one count of first-degree kidnapping. Prosecutors alleged that the charges arose from a videotape showing the repeated abuse of a girl who was about 2 years old at the time.

The appearance was brief and largely procedural. Stiles did not enter a plea to the accusations, and the judge ordered that he remain in custody without bail while the case moved toward a preliminary hearing. The charges were allegations; Stiles had not yet been tried or convicted.

### Videotape led to public search

The investigation began after a videotape was found in the Nevada desert and eventually turned over to law-enforcement authorities. The recording showed an adult man abusing a small child, but investigators initially did not know the identities of either the suspect or the victim.

Police released enhanced still photographs of the man and asked the public for help. The disturbing images received widespread television and online coverage, producing tips from people who believed they recognized him.

Elaine Thomas, who had previously been involved with Stiles, told investigators that the man in the images was Stiles. She said she recognized his face and other identifying characteristics and had no doubt about the identification. Her information gave detectives a name to pursue and helped turn the case from an unidentified-suspect investigation into a manhunt.

Police also identified the child and determined that the abuse had occurred several years earlier in the Las Vegas area. Investigators said Stiles had known the girl’s family and had access to the child.

### Arrest after police tip

After Stiles was publicly identified, authorities circulated his photograph and information nationally. He was arrested in the Las Vegas-area city of Henderson after police received information about his whereabouts and an officer spotted a man believed to be Stiles in a vehicle.

Officers stopped the vehicle and took him into custody without a prolonged confrontation. He was then booked and transferred to the Clark County jail to face the 23-count complaint.

The arrest ended several days of intense publicity surrounding the case. Police had warned that Stiles might try to hide or change his appearance after seeing his photograph in news reports.

### Statements from Elaine Thomas and Tina Allen

Thomas said she came forward because she recognized Stiles in the publicly released images. She described the identification as immediate and certain and said she wanted authorities to find him before another child could be harmed. She also spoke about her past relationship with Stiles and portrayed him as controlling and abusive.

Tina Allen, the victim’s mother, said Stiles had been a trusted family acquaintance who had been allowed around the child and, at times, to watch her. Allen said she had not known about the recorded assault when it happened and was devastated to learn what the tape showed.

Allen said her daughter, who was several years older by the time the case became public, appeared not to remember the abuse. She expressed relief that Stiles had been arrested but also anger that someone the family knew and trusted was accused of exploiting that access to the child. She said she wanted him held accountable and kept away from children.

The case attracted national attention both because of the child’s age and because investigators had used images from the recording to ask the public to identify the suspect. Authorities emphasized that the release of the still photographs—and the resulting identification by people who knew Stiles—was central to locating and arresting him.
